mostWorthwhile.text: Making the First star was most worthwhile: the dense-cloud sequence connected the mythic gesture to star formation, while explicitly distinguishing nuclear fusion from ordinary fire.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting Light and Gravity found no available partners, making the route forward less clear despite their apparent relevance to the goals.

surprise.text: Earth and Water made Pigment rather than an ingredient obviously connected to the cosmic goals; its image of colour awaiting a painter hinted at a later possibility.

arbitrary.text: Combining the First star with Air to make a Starfield felt less clearly motivated than gathering stars with Gravity; the result suggested repetition across space, but Air's role was unclear.

continue.text: Yes. The educational distinction about stellar fusion and the closing question about what stars can give besides light make me curious to see how the world develops.
